purpose: Distinguish the three put conflict-handling modes and the three channel definitions. Experiment 1 (duplicate put on main) separates INSERT OR IGNORE (no change, channel 0) from INSERT OR REPLACE / ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE (one change, channel 1) and reveals whether the channel counts direct row changes. Experiment 2 (put, begin, conflicting put, rollback) tests whether the channel counts uncommitted direct changes (changes()/total_changes) versus committed effects, and whether rollback restores the counter. Experiment 3 (put on main, conflicting put on other) separates main-only total_changes from main+other total_changes, since the other connection's change is invisible to main total_changes but visible to the combined channel. Together these three experiments separate all 18 family members: conflict mode by experiment 1, trigger presence by whether the channel exceeds the direct change count, and channel scope by experiments 2 and 3.
